Breadth-First Traversal (BFT) Also known as level-order traversal when applied to trees.
It starts at a node and explores all its immediate neighbors before moving on to child nodes.
Depth-First Traversal (DFT) Also known as depth-first search.
It starts at a node and explores as for as possible along one branch before backtracking to other branches.
Preorder Visit first root and then children.
preorder(node): if node is null: return visit(node) preorder(node.left) preorder(node.right) Inorder Visit first left child, then root, finally right child. Put root in-between children.
inorder(node): if node is null: return inorder(node.left) visit(node) inorder(node.right) Postorder Visit first left child, then right child, finally the root. Put root after children.
postorder(node): if node is null: return postorder(node.left) postorder(node.right) visit(node)
summary:
Breadth-First Traversal (BFT)

Also known as level-order traversal when applied to trees.

It starts at a node and explores all its immediate neighbors before moving on to child nodes.

Depth-First Traversal (DFT)

Also known as depth-first search.

It starts at a node and explores as for as possible along one branch before backtracking to other branches.

Preorder

Visit first root and then children.

preorder(node):
  if node is null:
    return

  visit(node)
  preorder(node.left)
  preorder(node.right)
Inorder

Visit first left child, then root, finally right child. Put root in-between children.
